golden_test_names: interpolates a heading that contains regex metacharacters
reproduction:
Extract the files at the commit under test (git show <sha>:packages/jest-each/src/table/array.ts and packages/jest-each/src/table/interpolation.ts), then:
  npm install typescript @types/node @jest/get-type pretty-format jest-regex-util
  npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
  node -e "const array=require('./out/array.js').default; console.log(JSON.stringify(array('rows: $count(*) is $expected',[{'count(*)':1,expected:'one'}]).map(r=>r.title)))"
At parent_commit this throws SyntaxError (Nothing to repeat); at fix_commit it prints ["rows: 1 is one"].
observed_failure_at_parent: SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /\$(count(*)|expected)[.\w]*/g: Nothing to repeat (thrown at collection time, so the whole .each table fails)
verified: both directions observed in bench-base:node-22: parent throws SyntaxError, fix prints ["rows: 1 is one"]; parent source confirmed to build the alternation with Object.keys(template).join('|') (no escaping, no sort) and fix source confirmed to use escapeStrForRegex + longest-first sort
install_recipe: For the monorepo oracle: corepack enable && yarn install && yarn build; then yarn jest packages/jest-each. Verified lightweight route (used here): npm install typescript @types/node '@jest/get-type' pretty-format jest-regex-util; extract the two src files at the commit; npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
issue_paraphrase: Writing a table-driven test whose column heading contains characters that are special in regular expressions (for example a heading like count(*)) makes the whole table blow up with a SyntaxError about an invalid regular expression before any test can run, and headings containing a dot or a pipe interpolate the wrong value instead of the column's text. Column headings should be usable literally inside $variable test titles.
fix_summary: Sort template keys longest-first and escape every key with jest-regex-util's escapeStrForRegex before joining them into the $variable alternation, so headers like 'count(*)' and 'a|b' are matched literally; when the template has no keys, fall back to only replacing $#.
notes: Verified with a two-file direct repro (packages/jest-each/src/table/array.ts + table/interpolation.ts, tsc-compiled) without building the monorepo. The e2e test (e2e/each/__tests__/specialCharacterKeys.test.js) needs a full build; the unit test packages/jest-each/src/__tests__/template.test.ts is the golden one. Node >= 22 used (node:util behavior irrelevant here; error is from the RegExp constructor).

golden_test_names: works like micromatch when options are passed after the same glob was used without them
works like micromatch when the same glob is used with different options
works like micromatch when a glob is used without options after being used with them
works like micromatch when dot is passed as undefined
reproduction:
Extract packages/jest-util/src/globsToMatcher.ts and packages/jest-util/src/replacePathSepForGlob.ts at the commit under test, then:
  npm install typescript @types/node picomatch@4
  npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
  node -e "const g=require('./out/globsToMatcher.js').default; console.log(g(['*.dotoption.js'])('.hidden.dotoption.js'), g(['*.dotoption.js'],{dot:false})('.hidden.dotoption.js'))"
At parent_commit this prints 'true true'; at fix_commit it prints 'true false' (the dot:false call must not match a dotfile). Both calls must happen in the same process because the stale matcher lives in the module-level cache.
observed_failure_at_parent: true true — the second call, made with {dot:false}, still returns true because the glob was cached during the first call (default dot:true) and the cache is keyed on the glob string only
verified: both directions observed in bench-base:node-22 with picomatch 4.0.7: parent returns true for the dot:false call, fix returns false; parent source confirmed to have the unconditional cache test 'if (!globsToMatchersMap.has(glob))' with no option-awareness, fix source confirmed to introduce 'const cacheable = picomatchOptions === undefined' and only serve/populate the cache when no options are passed
install_recipe: Monorepo oracle: corepack enable && yarn install && yarn build; then yarn jest packages/jest-util. Verified lightweight route (used here): npm install typescript @types/node picomatch@4; extract globsToMatcher.ts + replacePathSepForGlob.ts at the commit; npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
issue_paraphrase: File-selection behavior that depends on glob-matching options can silently stop working after the first time a pattern is seen: matchers are cached per pattern, so a glob first compiled with one option set (for example dotfile matching on) keeps behaving that way for every later request even when different options such as dot:false are passed. Patterns used for excluding or including files therefore match stale sets within the same run, depending on call order.
fix_summary: Only reuse or populate the module-level matcher cache when the caller passed no picomatchOptions; whenever options are given, build a fresh picomatch matcher with the caller's options (with the dot default = true preserved when dot is explicitly undefined). This makes globsToMatcher behave like micromatch across repeated calls with differing options.
notes: The module-level cache means the reproduction must do the two calls in one process (exactly what the golden tests do). The four new tests in packages/jest-util/src/__tests__/globsToMatcher.test.ts use distinct glob names so they are order-independent. globsToMatcher feeds jest-config normalize, SearchSource, shouldInstrument and HasteFS, i.e. test selection and coverage/transform inclusion. Verified with the two-file direct repro at picomatch 4.0.7 (= jest's ^4.0.3 pin).

golden_test_names: calls global test with title containing bigint param values
calls global test with title containing a cyclic %j param value
calls global test with title containing param values holding replacement patterns
reproduction:
Extract packages/jest-each/src/table/array.ts and packages/jest-each/src/table/interpolation.ts at the commit under test, then:
  npm install typescript @types/node @jest/get-type pretty-format
  npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
  node -e "const array=require('./out/array.js').default; console.log(JSON.stringify(array('expected string: %j %j %j %s',[[1n,{nested:2n},[3n],-4n]]).map(r=>r.title)))"
At parent_commit this throws TypeError (Do not know how to serialize a BigInt); at fix_commit it prints ["expected string: \"1n\" {\"nested\":\"2n\"} [\"3n\"] -4n"].
observed_failure_at_parent: TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt (thrown by util.format('%j', 1n); the whole .each definition fails)
verified: both directions observed in bench-base:node-22 (node v22.23.2): parent throws the BigInt TypeError when %j meets a bigint row value, fix renders the exact title the upstream regression test asserts; parent source confirmed to route %j through 'return util.format(formattedTitle, normalisedValue)' with no stringifyJson/interpolateJsonPlaceholder, fix source confirmed to intercept JSON_PLACEHOLDER with a custom stringifier that renders bigint as '${value}n' and cycles as '[Circular]'
install_recipe: Monorepo oracle: corepack enable && yarn install && yarn build; then yarn jest packages/jest-each (note this commit also touched packages/jest-core/src/lib/serializeToJSON.ts for --json bigint output; the golden jest-each tests only exercise packages/jest-each/src/table/array.ts). Verified lightweight route (used here): npm install typescript @types/node '@jest/get-type' pretty-format; extract table/array.ts + table/interpolation.ts at the commit; npx tsc --module commonjs --target es2022 --esModuleInterop --skipLibCheck --outDir out src/*.ts
issue_paraphrase: A table-driven test whose title uses the JSON placeholder %j crashes with TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt as soon as one of the row values is a bigint, so the whole test definition fails instead of producing a title. Titles should render bigint values as readable literals (like "1n"), and %j/%p titles should also not choke on cyclic values or on values that look like substitution patterns.
fix_summary: Intercept the %j placeholder inside jest-each's title formatter and serialize the value with a JSON stringifier that turns bigint into '<value>n' and cyclic structures into '[Circular]', instead of falling through to util.format which throws on bigint. Also switched %p (and %j) replacement from string patterns to replacer functions so values containing '$&', '$`', "$'" or '$$' are rendered literally. Symmetrically, jest-core's serializeToJSON gained a bigint converter for --json open-handles output.
notes: Verified with the two-file direct repro at node v22.23.2: the failure comes from util.format('%j', bigint) which throws on all modern Node (>= 18 behaves this way). The cyclic-%j and replacement-pattern tests in array.test.ts guard the same stringifier. The jest-core serializeToJSON half is only needed for --json CLI output, not for the golden jest-each tests. Full monorepo build (yarn install + yarn build) takes several minutes at 1 CPU; the targeted tsc repro avoids it entirely.
